claim: HeckeSevenEighths: the challenge's L-function is the paper's L_F(s, eta). For Re s > 1 the challenge defines it, by a Lean lemma, as (1/6) times the sum over nonzero alpha in O of chi(alpha) N(alpha)^(-s). The ring O = Z[omega] is a principal ideal domain whose six units act freely on its nonzero elements, so each nonzero ideal has exactly six generators. chi is trivial on units and the norm is unit-invariant, so each ideal contributes six equal terms, and the sum equals the sum over nonzero ideals a of eta(a) (Na)^(-s), with eta(alpha O) = chi(alpha); the rearrangement is valid by absolute convergence. The challenge's L-function is holomorphic off {0, 1}, so by the identity theorem the two functions agree on 7/8 < Re s <= 1.
